exercise.name: Cable Half Kneeling Face Pull

reference.title: Cable Half Kneeling Face Pull
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Cable machine (pulley at about head height)
exercise.mechanics: Compound (horizontal abduction, external rotation, scapular retraction, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the rope comes to the face, breathe in as the arms reach forward.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s pull, short hold, about 2 s return

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen and light: the shoulders must turn out fully at the finish.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a hold of 2 s at the face

cues.text: Half kneel on a mat facing the pulley, right knee down under the hip and left foot flat in front; hold the rope ends overhand, thumbs toward you, arms long at about face height.
Breathe out; pull the rope toward the face, elbows high and wide, then turn the shoulders out so the hands finish beside the ears.
Hands beside the ears, knuckles up, shoulder blades together; glute of the down leg tight.
Breathe in and let the arms reach forward under control.
Brief pause with the arms long, ribs down, then pull again.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to finish the pull
mistakes.fix: Stay tall over the down knee, glute tight.
Keep the elbows high, about level with the shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling to the chest without turning out
mistakes.fix: Finish with the hands beside the ears.
Use a weight you can hold at the face for a second.

kinematics.norm: About shoulder height at the finish (clinical opinion)
Upper arms back to about the frontal plane; posterior deltoid works in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013, Reinold 2007)
Forearms turned up at the finish; external rotation with the arm abducted loads the infraspinatus (Sung 2023)
From nearly straight to about 90 degrees or more (clinical opinion)
Tall half kneeling, pelvis level and still (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s pull and 2 s return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Half Kneeling Face Pull, video (movement reference)
Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)
Reinold et al. 2007, electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469)
Sung, Jung, Wang and Kim 2023, the effects of body positions and abduction angles on shoulder muscle activity patterns during external rotation exercises (Healthcare 11(14):1977)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move with the trunk still and the shoulders down.
Kneel on a mat; let the rope back to the stack before standing.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: lower the pulley to chest height and turn out less.
Knee discomfort: tall kneel on a thicker pad, or stand.

Elbows well bent at the finish
